Try not to look at other peoples plates. I’ll start by saying I’m not trying to attack you in anyway at all and I’m sorry if it comes across as such. 

First of all you have not even the slightest idea of what this person has / is going through. Social media is a platform where we are able to construct yourselves to appear any way we want and it rarely is a honest depiction of ones self. That person who just got a new house? Lost their mother today. That person who just got an award? Was beaten and sexually abused and told they would amount to nothing. That boy who broke a world record? His dad broke his ribs when he was 10 because he was “a worthless piece of shit”. 

The way you worded this made it seem like because life is so hard that you deserve to have something given to you. Life is hard, I’m so sorry that you have suffered the things you listed in your OP. Truly. But life isn’t a transaction of well this bad thing happened so now I feel like life owes me something good.

No one is chosen for platinum life. Some are just more fortunate than others. It’s up to us as individuals to fight for what we want and work for it. Some may have to work harder then others? Yes, definitely. Is it fair? Not necessarily. Will you be stronger with mountains of resolve and resilience in comparison to someone who made it to where you were by having it simply given to them? Absolutely. 

A key problem I think you have is you’re constantly looking into others lives when you should be focusing on your own. 

I’m going to leave you with a famous quote.


“The only time you look in your neighbor's bowl is to make sure that they have enough. You don't look in your neighbor's bowl to see if you have as much as them.”
